# The Pre-History

## Why it exists

> status: ratified (D-0015, D-0056)

The collapse needs a before. The pre-history carries allegory-framed big ideas with
major consequences, so the audience deeply understands what changed, what was lost,
and what limited possibilities remain. It is not nostalgia: knowing the before is
what makes the present legible and the future imaginable.

## The equilibrium

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The working sketch ([[the-old-balance]]): before enclosure, survival was a strict,
unsentimental negotiation with the land. Small spoken proofs justified each taking; a
village that over-fished or over-felled faced the Wyrd's impartial correction. It was
not a golden age — it was hard, dangerous, and balanced. The magic of the era was a
daily tool of subsistence, not a weapon.

## The original sin

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The fall was an economic decision, not a dark rite ([[first-storehouse-lie]]): keepers
of a communal surplus declined, one spring, to give it back. To hold the hoard against
the land's own law, they commissioned the first false proof — the fiction that fenced
ground stands outside the web of reciprocity. It worked, mostly. The remainder — the
first axiomatic debt — seeped into the soil around the storehouse and was deemed an
acceptable cost.

## The boiling frog

> status: provisional (D-0072)

No apocalypse day: generations of creep. Each success of the first lie invited a
larger one — fields, forests, rivers, valleys — each fenced behind a fresh fiction,
each fiction's debt pushed downhill and downstream. The keepers became lords; the
false proofs compounded into a legal cosmos ([[the-empire]]); the sourness in the
land stopped being deniable roughly when it stopped being survivable, by which time
the people who could have spoken the counter-proofs had been hunted for two centuries
([[breaking-of-the-stones]], [[information-control]]).

## What was lost, what remains

> status: ratified (D-0013, D-0056)

The losses are permanent on any human timescale: there is no magical reset, and even
total victory over the empire leaves a changed world. What remains: pockets of
balance, buried archives, fragment-holders, the unbounded capacity of taught minds —
and the precedent of every previous cycle that some people, somewhere, built something
better on the far side ([[cycles]]).
